nodes.label: first five minutes
nodes.instruction:
Someone emailed about an IT problem. Read troubleshooting/mickey-playbook.md first, then the whole email thread.
Do the first-five-minutes checks (playbook §3): who and what is affected (one user, one customer, or many), where it lives (§1), whether its host is OK, and whether something changed just before (recent cluster tasks, a deploy, the 21:00–01:00 Melbourne backup window).
Post what you found in this chat before you change anything. Never print passwords, keys, tokens or .env files.
Report ours if it's a system in §1. Report hand_over if it isn't in §1, or if many things are failing at once (likely a host, a router or NEXTDC). Report no_action if it's only for information, an alert that has already cleared, or spam.
nodes.success: We know who and what is affected and whether it's ours, and the findings are in this chat.

results.name: ours
results.meaning: it's a system Mickey can reach (§1)

results.name: hand_over
results.meaning: not ours, or many things failing at once

results.name: no_action
results.meaning: nothing to do: for information, already cleared, or spam

nodes.label: find the fault
nodes.instruction:
Find the fault using the playbook section for {system} (§4 VMs, §5 Maptco SAP, §6 phones, §7 CVP2, §8 BE Hub, §9 Bepoz).
Only look: logs, status and config. Follow every rule in §2: never restart anything carrying live calls, never touch the routers or the never-touch list, no logins to live Bepoz SQL.
When you know the fix, write it up in this chat as:
What's broken: <who/what, since when>
Checked: <commands run and what they showed>
I think: <your best guess>
Suggest: <the fix, and whose OK it needs (§11)>
Report allowed only if the fix is starting a service that has already stopped (an SAP service, the Shopify sync, BE Agent, b2brestapi). Report needs_ok for any other change. Report cleared if it's working now and nothing needs changing. Report stuck if you've spent 15 minutes and don't know where the fault is, or it turns out not to be ours.
nodes.success: The fault and the suggested fix are written up in this chat, or it's working again, or we know we're stuck.

results.name: allowed
results.meaning: the fix is starting a service that has already stopped

results.name: needs_ok
results.meaning: the fix needs Martin's or Joy's OK

results.name: cleared
results.meaning: it's working now, nothing to change

results.name: stuck
results.meaning: fault not found in 15 minutes, or not ours

nodes.label: OK to fix?
nodes.question: Martin or Joy: Mickey's findings and suggested fix are just above in this chat (What's broken / Checked / I think / Suggest). Should Mickey make the change?

nodes.label: make the fix
nodes.instruction:
Make only the fix that was agreed in this chat (or, without an OK, only start the service that had stopped).
Before a real change to a VM, snapshot it: qm snapshot <vmid> pre-<what>-<date>. For a small in-guest config edit, back up the file instead.
Then check it worked, the same way you found the fault.
Say in this chat what you changed and how you checked it. If you started a stopped service without an OK, tell Martin or Joy.
nodes.success: The change is made and checked, and this chat says what changed and how it was checked.

results.name: failed
results.meaning: the fix didn't work or couldn't be made

nodes.label: tell the reporter
nodes.instruction:
Email the person who reported it (for approval): what was wrong and what was done, or that it's working now and nothing needed changing. Ask them to reply if it's still not right.
Plain words: no commands, IP addresses or secrets. Sign off as "Mickey, BE IT support". Never claim to be a person.

nodes.label: read their reply
nodes.instruction:
They wrote back. Read the new message.
If it's still not working, or there's a new symptom, post it in this chat and report still_broken.
If they say it's working, or just thank us, report ok.
nodes.success: We know whether it's fixed for them.

results.name: still_broken
results.meaning: still not working, or a new symptom

nodes.label: hand over
nodes.instruction:
Hand this to a person (playbook §10). In this chat, tag Martin or Joy with:
What's broken: <who/what, since when>
Checked: <commands run and what they showed>
I think: <your best guess, or "don't know">
Suggest: <the fix, and whose OK it needs>
and say whether the ops session should take it.
Then email the person who reported it (for approval) that someone at BE is taking it over. Sign off as "Mickey, BE IT support".
nodes.success: Martin or Joy has the hand-over note in this chat, and the reporter knows a person is taking it.
